title: Rotating Specialist Pools and Sprint Shelving Guidelines for Mid-Cycle Reprioritization
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Define a lightweight operational protocol for forming short-lived rotating specialist pools and a sprint-shelving mechanism to enable safe mid-cycle reprioritization without creating long-lived technical debt or blocking mission-critical work.

Why: We frequently need to reallocate scarce expert time (model infra, kernel engineers, infra SREs, privacy reviewers) to urgent cross-team work mid-cycle. Current ad-hoc swaps cause ownership confusion, stalled rollouts, and uneven on-call coverage. This policy provides guardrails so PMs can request swarms, eng leads can allocate, and design/review obligations are conserved.

Goals:
- Create a 2-week rotating specialist pool pattern with clear onboarding, handoff, and rollback rules.
- Define sprint-shelving criteria to pause lower-priority scope and reclaim 10-30% of specialist effort for higher priority initiatives.
- Minimize coordination cost: single Slack channel + single cycle tracker row per pool.
- Preserve code health: require pre-shelving cleanup criteria and post-shelve re-evaluation windows.

Scope includes: model-serving performance hotfixes, Dedicated autoscale incidents requiring infra specialists, short-run private/VPC compliance asks (audit support), and high-ROI console experiments requiring design critique. Not intended for long-term reprioritization (multicycle scope moves).

Key protocol elements:
1) Pool formation: PM files a short request (template below) and tags the owning engineering lead. Pool duration defaults to 2 weeks (can be extended once by mutual consent). Pool size guided by a 20%-of-squad heuristic for specialists; absolute caps: 1 for single-owner repos, 3 for cross-team features.

2) Sprint shelving: PM/eng decide which backlog items to shelve. Shelved items must meet three criteria: no external customer SLA regression, no open security/PGP issues, and no active customer escalations pinned to them. Shelving is a pause, not abandonment — items move to a "shelved" swimlane and get a "revisit window" date.

3) Onboarding checklist for rotating specialists (must be completed within first 24 hours): access granted, one-sentence ownership statement in ticket, key context links, current test/benchmark artifacts, and a rollback plan stub.

4) Handoff + knowledge capture: At pool end, owner writes a 1-paragraph summary + 3 follow-ups and attaches CI/regression artifacts. If work carries beyond pool, the owning team must nominate a long-term owner before the pool dissolves.

Trade-offs considered:
- Fragmentation risk vs velocity: rotation increases throughput on urgent work but can fragment code knowledge. Mitigation: short rotations + mandatory handoff.
- Specialist churn vs team morale: frequent reassignments can be disruptive. Mitigation: cap rotation frequency to once per 4 cycles per individual unless volunteer.

Operational artifacts and links:
- Request template: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A-rotating-pool-template
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3245
- Console dashboard for pool utilization: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pools/rotating-specialist-utilization
- Cycle tracker row example: https://sheets.redwood.ai/cycle-tracker#row=874316

Decision records:
- 2025-02-10: Agreed on 2-week default duration (decision note in Google Doc).
- 2025-02-13: Engineering requested a maximum of one extension per pool to avoid indefinite assignments.

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: Publish policy + templates; update Cycle Playbook; host 45-min office hours for PM/Eng leads.
- Week 2: Pilot with 2 pools (Serving Runtime kernel optimizations and Dedicated autoscale knob).
- End of Week 3: Collect quantitative metrics (time-to-assign specialist, #shelved tickets, regression incidents) and qualitative feedback.

Metrics to evaluate success:
- Median time from request to specialist assignment (target <48h).
- Percentage of shelved tickets reactivated without extra rework (target >80%).
- Specialist satisfaction (pulse survey) and number of unplanned regressions tied to pool work.

Rollout guardrails:
- Prohibit shelving of work tied to active customer SLO reductions or audits.
- For enterprise customers with active escalations, require customer-success signoff before any shelving.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Playbook published and linked from cycle onboarding docs.
- Two pilot pools run and documented.
- Dashboard capturing assignment & revisit-window metrics available.
